content: Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the medications you are currently using, including both prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as any herbal products. This medication should not be taken alongside other medications that contain abacavir. Carefully check the labels of all your prescription medications to ensure they do not contain abacavir. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. If the situation is not life-threatening, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load measurements, and T-cell counts. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store abacavir tablets or solution at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The liquid form of this medication can also be stored in the refrigerator but should not be frozen. Over time, the solution may change color from clear or yellow to brown, which is normal. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: In some patients, abacavir has been associated with a serious, and sometimes fatal, allergic reaction. Your doctor should perform a blood test to assess your risk before starting this medication or restarting it after a break. If the test indicates a higher risk, you should not take this medication, and your doctor will discuss alternative treatment options with you. Symptoms of an allergic reaction may include rash, itching or swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, difficulty breathing, fever, extreme fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, muscle aches, sore throat, or cough. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of these symptoms. If you have stopped taking abacavir due to an allergic reaction, you must never take it again, as this could result in death. Inform all your doctors and pharmacists if you have discontinued abacavir due to an allergic reaction. Properly dispose of any unused abacavir. Uses: This medication is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. However, abacavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide and Warning Card provided by your pharmacist before starting abacavir and each time you get a refill. Carry the Warning Card with you at all times. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. If you are using the liquid form, carefully measure the dose using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you stop taking abacavir, even for a short time, and then restart it, you have an increased risk of developing a very serious, potentially fatal allergic reaction. Refill your medication before you run out. Do not stop treatment unless directed by your doctor. It is crucial to take this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed. Do not skip doses, increase your dose, or take this drug more frequently than prescribed without consulting your doctor. For the best effect, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Side Effects: Difficulty sleeping or loss of appetite may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Rarely, this medication has caused severe, and sometimes fatal, liver problems and a buildup of lactic acid in the blood (lactic acidosis). These serious side effects are more common in women and obese patients. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking abacavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Abacavir may increase your risk of a heart attack. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as ways to lower your risk of heart disease. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of passing HIV infection to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication must not be taken with other medications that contain abacavir. Check the labels on all your other prescription medications to ensure they do not contain abacavir.
